title: Grace freely given and grace that makes pleasing
source_text: XI. Porro gratia quae per Christum homini corrupto confertur, communiter in Schola Romana distingui solet, in gratiam quam vocant gratis datam, & in gratiam gratum facientem. Quae partitio, ex Doctorum Scholae istius mente, sic accipienda non est, quasi aliqua sit gratia non gratis data; nam quam vocant gratum facientem agnoscunt etiam esse gratuito donatam: Sed quod alibi saepe fit, uni speciei quae proprio nomine caret, relinquunt nomen generis, ut monet Bellarminus loco supra citato.
pass_a_gloss: XI. Further the grace which through Christ is conferred on corrupted man, is commonly in the Roman School wont to be distinguished, into the grace which they call freely given, and into the grace making pleasing. Which partition, from the mind of the Doctors of that School, is not to be so taken, as though there were some grace not freely given; for that which they call making pleasing they acknowledge also to be gratuitously given: But as elsewhere often happens, to one species which lacks its proper name, they leave the name of the genus, as Bellarmine warns in the place above cited.
pass_b_english: Thesis XI. The grace conferred on corrupt man through Christ is commonly divided in the Roman School into what they call grace freely given and the grace that makes pleasing.
In the minds of that School's doctors the division is not meant to imply that some grace is not freely given, for they grant that the grace that makes pleasing is also given freely.
Rather, as often happens elsewhere, one species that has no name of its own is left with the name of the genus, as Bellarmine points out in the place cited above.
